subject: Post-demo: Anchor Retail embeddings integration — technical recap & proposed next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: Anchor Retail embeddings integration — technical recap & proposed next steps

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — great demo and helpful context on the search/recommendation workloads. Quick recap + proposed path forward so we can align on the engineering work. I’ve attached the recording and a short sizing proposal.

Call highlights (short):
- Current system: 12M SKUs, ~1.2M unique product descriptions, hosted vector index (VectraCloud) that you want to replace for latency/cost reasons.
- Primary use-cases: (1) product-to-product recommendations (online), (2) semantic search for merchandising/editor tools (internal), (3) periodic reranking for top-N blends.
- QPS: you estimated 120 QPS peak for retrieval and ~600 writes/hr for batch updates.

Initial technical recommendations (opinionated):
- Embedding model & dimension: start with 1536-d embeddings (redwood-embed-2) for retrieval + reranker compatibility. If storage cost is a hard cap we can evaluate a 1024-d variant in A/B.
- Normalization: L2-normalize vectors at write time; store pre-normalized vectors to use dot-product search equivalently to cosine with better numeric stability.
- Batching: ingestion: use batched upserts at 256 vectors/batch with 4 concurrent workers for steady-state ingestion; for bulk backfill we’ll use 1024-element batches to speed throughput. Retrieval: dynamic batching for multi-query pipelines — start conservative (per-request latency budget) and scale up as we test.
- Migration approach: dual-write for new items + backfill reindex for historical docs. We recommend a short canary reindex (1M items) to validate ranking before full cutover.
- Auth/routing: Redwood SDK supports API-key-based auth and VPC routing to your preferred region. For Anchor Retail private deployment we can propose an IAM-based option if needed.
- Reranker: preserve current reranker (model-based) as a post-retrieval step during canary; recommend a hybrid blend (retrieval then rerank) for relevance-sensitive flows.

Open questions for you (please reply inline):
1) Confirm peak QPS numbers and typical query size (avg tokens/terms) so we can refine batch sizing and latency targets.
2) Do you need per-region data residency (EU/APAC)? You mentioned US-first but want clarity.
3) Any constraints on temporary reindex window (how long can you tolerate indexing traffic)?

Next steps (proposed):
- Internal: Redwood will draft a one-page migration plan and a short cost delta estimate for 1536 vs 1024 dims (Ben + Evelyn to own).
- External: Oliver / Priya to share current index stats CSV (counts, avg dims, current storage) and any retention constraints.
- Schedule: propose a 30-min technical kickoff early next week to align infra owners.

Attachments: anchorretail-demo-recording.mp4, anchor-embed-sizing-proposal.pdf

Thanks — Sean

Sean —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below and attaching current-index-stats.csv.

Answers:
1) Peak retrieval QPS: 110-130 (spikes to 180 during promos). Typical query is short (2–6 tokens) for user search; merchandising queries are longer (20–100 tokens).
2) Data residency: US only for now; open to EU later but not immediate.
3) Reindex window: we can accept up to 48 hours of increased indexing traffic during a migration weekend; production write traffic cannot be paused.

On dimensions: Curious if 1536 is required; our current provider uses a 1024-d model. If 1536 gives a clear ranking improvement we can do it, but storage is a factor.

Other notes: security team asks whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and if you have SOC2 Type II evidence — we’ll need that for procurement.

On Thu, Mar 9, 2028 at 6:10 PM Oliver White <oliver.white@anchorretail.com> wrote:
> Sean —
> 
> Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below and attaching current-index-stats.csv.

Quick internal notes / proposal (Evelyn feel free to correct):

- Dimension decision: Recommend defaulting to 1536 for the canary. Rationale: it buys headroom for reranker features and blended search; we can quantize to int8/fp16 storage profiles during ingestion to reduce cost. If Anchor’s cost gate prevents 1536 we’ll run a controlled A/B with 1024 and compare recall@K and reranker delta on a holdout set.
- Migration plan sketch:
  1) Canary: pick a 1M item slice (merchandising + hot products) -> index with Redwood (1536) -> run parallel reranker experiments for 72 hours.
  2) Dual-write: instrument producer to write to both VectraCloud and Redwood for 14 days.
  3) Backfill: reindex remaining corpus in 48–72 hours (weekend heavy IO window).
- Batching & throughput:
  * Bulk backfill: 1024 vectors / request, concur 8 workers (network-bound), use compression on payloads.
  * Steady-state ingestion: 256 vectors / request, concur 4 workers, exponential retry on throttles.
- Auth: Redwood supports API key for hosted deployments; for Dedicated/Private we can integrate KMS-backed keys. Provide SOC2 and KMS whitepaper in procurement packet.
- Routing/latency: put primary read replicas in us-east-1 to serve east coast traffic, with optional edge-caching for read-heavy merchandising endpoints.

Action items for Sean to send to Anchor: Draft canary scope + timeline, cost delta spreadsheet, list of API calls and example SDK snippets for quickstart.

Evelyn — can you add a short note on expected tokenization/embedding latency per vector (estimate) and any SDK setup quirks we should call out?

Thanks, Ben

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Following up with short technical clarifications and a proposed small playbook to make the migration low-friction. I’ve pasted the critical bits below and linked a one-page plan.

Quick clarifications: 
- Embedding latency: redwood-embed-2 average encode time is ~8–12ms/vector on our hosted runtime (p99 ~40ms) depending on token length. For bulk backfills this is amortized by batching and GPU throughput.
- SDK setup (quickstart): use the Redwood Python SDK:
  - pip install redwood-sdk
  - client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<YOUR_KEY>")
  - emb = client.embeddings.create(model="redwood-embed-2", input=doc_text)
  - upsert to vector store via client.vectors.upsert(namespace="anchor-products", vectors=[...])
- Auth & keys: we support API keys, KMS-integrated keys for Dedicated, and HSM-backed key management for Private deployments. Procurement pack (SOC2 + KMS whitepaper) available on request.
- Normalization & quantization: we recommend L2-normalize at client/worker time. For storage savings, convert to fp16 before writing to vector DB; Redwood’s ingestion supports this conversion in-flight.
- Reranker flow: keep your existing reranker in the loop for the canary. Redwood will return top-100 candidates; run reranker on that set and report recall/CTR delta.

Minimal migration playbook (one-page):
1) Kickoff meeting (T+0): confirm canary slice and ownership.
2) Canary index (T+1–T+3): index 1M items, run parallel telemetry for 72 hours.
3) Evaluate (T+4): compare reranker metrics and latency, decide go/no-go.
4) Dual-write (T+5–T+19): dual-write live traffic to both systems.
5) Backfill & cutover (T+20–T+22): full reindex and switch over after smoke tests.

Deliverables we’ll share by Monday:
- Detailed one-page plan (Doc link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDAnchorEmbedPlan)
- Cost delta spreadsheet (1536 vs 1024 dims)
- Short SDK quickstart snippet and curl examples
- Procure: SOC2 attestation and KMS whitepaper

If that sounds good I’ll schedule the 30-min kickoff for next Tue morning (US) and include infra/ops contacts.

Best —
